name: change_propagation_ripple_effect_analysis

metrics: Precision/recall of impact sets; ripple-effect size.
relation_to_us: Directly comparable to our parent-only dependency-graph expansion (B3 Graph@K) and to the proposed graph escalation arm.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - change-propagation is a classical adjacent line; ours is intent-conditioned selection on real commits with an explicit budget gate.
idea_to_test: Test: change-propagation-style closure (multi-hop reachability over the frozen graph) as a cheap B3-graph alternative on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
status: SEEDED - concept verified; no single canonical system; cite the classical line
notes: No canonical single 'RIPPLE' paper/venue; the row means the ripple-effect/change-propagation analysis line. Verified the classical basis only.

name: RepoCoder_RepoAgent_memory_conditioned_generation
mechanism: Iterative retrieval-generation pipeline with a repository memory (similarity-based retriever + code LM); clones-like memory conditioning.
evidence: RepoCoder verified (EMNLP 2023): repo-level code completion, >10% over in-file baseline on RepoEval.
relation_to_us: Adjacent to the planner/agent line and to memory-conditioned iteration; our snapshot-conditioned cheap ranking is the zero-LLM counterpart.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - memory-conditioned iteration is established; not a direct threat to cost-aware escalation.
idea_to_test: Test: none immediately; monitor as a stronger LLM baseline under a fresh confirmatory protocol.
notes: 'Repository Memory' row mapped to RepoCoder (verified). RepoAgent (arXiv 2402.16670) still SEEDED. Reid & Neubig ICML 2024 repo-prompt work noted.

name: adaptive_top-k_and_adaptive_kNN
mechanism: Query-adaptive retrieval depth / query-specific neighborhood size instead of a fixed K.
evidence: Shichao Zhang KNN line verified (Challenges in KNN TKDE 2022; One-step TKDE 2021; Adaptive kNN graph 2026). IR/RAG adaptive retrieval is a known pattern (no single primary source).
relation_to_us: Directly motivates 'K is an operating-point curve, not a final configuration' and the adaptive-K rules in the omission-risk study.
novelty_threat: LOW-MEDIUM - adaptive-k is a known pattern; our contribution is applying it to repository change localization under an explicit budget.
idea_to_test: Test: fixed-K vs adaptive-K routing on TRAIN/VALIDATION (done in omission-risk study v1: no benefit over fixed-10).
status: SEEDED - pattern verified via the Zhang line; no single IR primary source pinned

name: Graph-guided_localization_agent
mechanism: Graph-guided agent: dynamic AST+call graph, search/fix phases; localization file ranking as found_files.
evidence: Direct evidence (P5-B/P5-C): 10/10 held-out, 5 empty, 402 calls/32.8M tokens/$9.93 est.
datasets: djangoCMS real commits (shared protocol); upstream SWE-bench-style.
relation_to_us: Primary external comparator under the shared protocol.
novelty_threat: HIGH - the graph-guided agent is the natural 'strong' baseline for selective escalation; cost is the differentiator.
idea_to_test: Test: reuse as the expensive verifier in a future selective-escalation design (not now).

name: GraphLocator_causal_issue_graph_localization
mechanism: LLM-based issue localization via a causal issue graph (CIG): symptom-vertex locating then dynamic CIG expansion over code dependency graphs; decomposes sub-issues, models causal dependencies.
evidence: Verified primary source: function-level recall/precision gains over retrieval baselines on Python+Java SWE-bench-style data; graph improves downstream issue resolution.
relation_to_us: Directly comparable to our graph-guided escalation arm and to the causal-expansion intuition behind omission-risk features; a strong close competitor.
novelty_threat: HIGH - the closest graph-guided localization competitor to our selective-escalation line.
idea_to_test: Test: contrast its causal-graph expansion intuition vs our cheap graph features; adopt causal-expansion as a future escalation design (documented; not executed).
notes: Corrects the previous CROSS-DOMAIN/bug-localization characterization: it is LLM-based causal graph reasoning for issue localization (FSE 2026).

name: RepoGraph_repo_level_code_graph_for_LLM
mechanism: Plug-in module managing a repository-level code graph (AST-derived) as guidance/navigation for AI software engineering; graph conditions agentic localization/generation.
evidence: Verified primary source: plugging RepoGraph into four SWE-bench methods boosts all; SOTA among open-source frameworks; CrossCodeEval extension.
metrics: SWE-bench resolve; retrieval hit; task completion.
relation_to_us: Directly comparable to our dependency-graph construction; their graph is a navigation aid for LLMs, ours is a frozen parent-only AST graph for cheap ranking/escalation.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - richer graph construction could inform our graph features; our cheap-seed finding already bounds graph-expansion value on the lexical signal.
idea_to_test: Test: whether a richer graph (call+inheritance edges) changes B3/Hybrid/omission-risk graph features on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: Corrects venue from 'ICSE 2024' to ICLR 2025 (arXiv comment).

name: Agentless_localization_then_repair
mechanism: Decoupled two-phase pipeline: localize (file+line) then repair WITHOUT agentic search loops; each phase one LLM call.
evidence: Verified primary source: SWE-bench Lite 32.00% (96 fixes) at $0.70, highest among open-source agents at the time; SWE-bench Lite-S introduced.
relation_to_us: Strong evidence that 'localize first, no agent loop' is competitive - the same philosophy as our sparse first pass + selective verification.
novelty_threat: HIGH - 'agentless' localization-first is a direct conceptual competitor to graph/agent escalation being necessary.
idea_to_test: Test: our BM25 first-pass + selective verification vs 'agentless-style' single-shot LLM localization on TRAIN/VALIDATION (fair-comparison boundary).
notes: arXiv 2407.01489 v2 (2024-10-29). Preprint; later venue status OPEN.
